heading: Single-direction refusal control in reasoning models remains contested
definition: whether V1 holds in models that reason before answering.
summary: Independent groups report both successful refusal control and failed single-direction ablations in reasoning models. Conflicting results on the same checkpoints use different methods, so the source of disagreement remains unresolved.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy and <1B: no studies (counts V8.studies_by_size has no such keys). 1-10B: C. Groups other than the original's, with recipes the pack marks close to the original, fail to remove refusal on Qwen3-8B (arXiv:2607.02396, harmful-minus-harmless DIM k=1 weight edit on a 4-bit NF4 model; https://openreview.net/forum?id=TynYvwkSlF, ablation during the CoT only) and on Qwen3.5-9B (arXiv:2605.21706, official DiM pipeline, no untreated baseline; https://openreview.net/forum?id=TynYvwkSlF). On Qwen3-8B, removal is reported with other methods: the original group's refused-minus-complied direction (arXiv:2507.03167, R1), all-layer ablation (https://openreview.net/forum?id=ySFIGhpfDe, text and figure only) and removal of a pre-decision direction (https://openreview.net/forum?id=TynYvwkSlF SubSteerDA, 0.89). DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B: removal in arXiv:2507.03167 (R1); partial with the original weight-orthogonalisation code (arXiv:2604.02574, 45.4%->26.2%); compliance 0.75->0.58 under CoT-only ablation (https://openreview.net/forum?id=TynYvwkSlF); from 0%, up to 39% (EOI direction) or 43% (EOT direction) with the CoT fixed, and 94% (EOI direction) with it regenerated under one-layer steering (arXiv:2605.26772). DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B addition: induction with a direction transplanted from Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (gh:anki079/refusal-in-reasoning-models) against a null with the model's own direction (gh:natalimuca/jailbreak-activation-detection), both README-only. Every same-checkpoint pair differs in method. 10-100B: C. GPT-OSS-20B: the only reported single-direction removal is the original group's (arXiv:2507.03167, R1: refused-minus-complied direction, per-expert weight orthogonalisation). Other groups fail with activation-level ablation or an unstated implementation (arXiv:2609.14759, lw:HfXyF4swFLpeLuv3W, arXiv:2605.21706, https://openreview.net/forum?id=TynYvwkSlF CoT-only). Qwen3-14B: two harmful-minus-harmless DIM tests by other groups disagree. Activation ablation succeeds (arXiv:2510.26418, JailbreakBench ASR 11%->91%), while a weight edit on a 4-bit NF4 model scored on HarmBench by LLM judges fails (arXiv:2607.02396, ASR 0.06 as a fraction). Phi-4-15B fails (arXiv:2605.21706, no untreated baseline). Qwen3.5-27B: gh:drewstone/safety-is-a-policy (README-only) gives ~30% compliance after abliteration and 0% with partial projections; arXiv:2608.17202 also reports failure but is unverified (its check was not returned). Qwen3-32B over-refusal (arXiv:2608.22490, weight edit) and GLM-4.7-Flash (arXiv:2609.32434, direction from refusal probes minus matched non-refusal writing requests, not harmful minus harmless) support. >100B: ?. There is no activation-level removal (counts V8.coverage_by_operation.removal.by_size has no >100B key). There are only multi-direction weight edits (arXiv:2608.17202 on Qwen3.5-122B and GLM-4.5-Air; unverified, its check was not returned), qualitative README outcomes (gh:jcartu/glm5.2-unbound) and steering (https://openreview.net/forum?id=qSmUharVw6).
suggested_status.reason: The original arXiv:2406.11717 did not test reasoning models (counts V8.original_sources_linked is empty). arXiv:2507.03167 shares an author with the original, so its results are the original group's extension (R1), not an independent reproduction. It reports removal in four models with a refused-minus-complied direction from end-of-prompt or CoT tokens, applied by hooks or weight edits, e.g. GPT-OSS-20B 93.4%->3.5% by per-expert weight orthogonalisation. Other groups report removal or induction with harmful-versus-harmless (or harmful-versus-benign) directions: arXiv:2510.26418 (Qwen3-14B ASR 11%->91%; benign compliance 94%->1% under addition), arXiv:2608.22490 (Qwen3-32B weight edit, over-refusal benchmarks) and arXiv:2607.02396 (Qwen3-1.7B DIM k=1 ASR 0.20->0.80 as fractions). arXiv:2609.32434 (GLM-4.7-Flash thinking, 5/5->0/5) instead builds its direction from refusal probes minus matched non-refusal writing requests. Other groups' single-direction ablations, with recipes the pack marks close to the original, fail on GPT-OSS-20B (arXiv:2609.14759, 4% coherent flips; lw:HfXyF4swFLpeLuv3W; arXiv:2605.21706; https://openreview.net/forum?id=TynYvwkSlF), on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B (arXiv:2607.02396, DIM ASR 0.07 and 0.06 as fractions) and on Qwen3.5-9B and Phi-4-15B (arXiv:2605.21706). These are failed replications, hence C. But no V8 conflict pairs two studies with the same method (same_method is n in all of them). On GPT-OSS-20B the only single-direction removal is the original group's per-expert weight edit, set against activation-level or unstated-implementation failures. The closest pair is Qwen3-14B, where activation ablation scored on JailbreakBench (arXiv:2510.26418) is set against a weight edit on a 4-bit NF4 model scored on HarmBench by LLM judges (arXiv:2607.02396). So the failures may come from method rather than model. counts: V8.verdicts.supports.studies 26, V8.verdicts.limits_scope.studies 23, V8.verdicts.challenges.studies 9. counts.json predates the checks. In the pack, the challenges verdicts come from arXiv:2609.14759, gh:natalimuca/jailbreak-activation-detection, lw:HfXyF4swFLpeLuv3W, arXiv:2609.03887, arXiv:2605.21706, arXiv:2607.02396, gh:drewstone/safety-is-a-policy, https://openreview.net/forum?id=TynYvwkSlF and arXiv:2503.11185. The check says arXiv:2503.11185's verdict should be none: RFA found no direction in DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, so nothing was ablated. lw:ixJrmYrgHM4TenN7D's V8 verdict in the pack is limits_scope, so it is not among them.
suggested_status.open_questions: (1) Plain all-layer harmful-minus-harmless ablation run with one pipeline and one judge on GPT-OSS-20B, Qwen3-8B/14B, Qwen3.5-9B and an R1-distill. It would need thinking on and off, coherence (non-completion) and capability measured, and both an activation hook and a weight edit. That would show whether the conflicts come from method (placement, extraction token, direction contrast, edit form, quantization, coherence filter) or from the models. On GPT-OSS-20B the only single-direction removal so far is the original group's (arXiv:2507.03167), so a single-direction removal there by another group would also change that cell. (2) Matched comparisons that separate reasoning training from size and from architecture. arXiv:2607.02396's authors say k=1 is insufficient for models of 8B and up; the same DIM k=1 edit gives 0.20->0.80 on Qwen3-1.7B and 0.02->0.51 on Qwen3-4B (fractions). Architecture: MoE GPT-OSS and hybrid DeltaNet Qwen3.5 (raised by gh:drewstone/safety-is-a-policy). (3) Any activation-level single-direction test above 100B. (4) Whether refusal persists inside the reasoning trace when the final answer complies.

source.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
source.authors: Andy Arditi; Oscar Obeso; Aaquib Syed; Daniel Paleka; Nina Panickssery; Wes Gurnee; Neel Nanda

original_result.result: The original paper did not test reasoning models.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Activation-level ablation of a single direction in reasoning models above 100B. At >100B the pack has only multi-direction weight edits (arXiv:2608.17202 Qwen3.5-122B, GLM-4.5-Air), qualitative README outcomes (gh:jcartu/glm5.2-unbound GLM-5.2) and steering (https://openreview.net/forum?id=qSmUharVw6 GPT-OSS-120B).

wording_issues.issue: The version is a question with no polarity, and results split by model, even on the same checkpoint. Counts V8.verdicts: supports 26 studies, limits_scope 23, challenges 9. GPT-OSS-20B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B and R1-Distill models each have both supporting and failing results (see conflicts). A yes/no reading cannot fit.

Studies cover very different set-ups: hybrid models with thinking toggled (Qwen3, Qwen3.5, GLM), R1-distilled models, RL-trained GPT-OSS, recurrent-depth Ouro Thinking, and authors' own Ra-SFT fine-tunes. Reasoning is sometimes only inferred (gh:sipratt-p/refusal-ablation-eval from judging notes) or not described during evaluation (arXiv:2601.16034). Several rows mark stage 'not stated' or 'instruct' for models the verdicts treat as reasoning (counts V8.studies_by_stage not stated: 10). One model behaves differently with thinking on and off (gh:jcartu/glm5.2-unbound).

wording_issues.phrase: a difference-in-means direction (harmful minus harmless instructions)
wording_issues.issue: Positive results in reasoning models also come from directions that differ from V1's in contrast, construction or extraction site. Other contrasts: ACT-model-minus-base (arXiv:2605.28467), refused-minus-complied (arXiv:2610.15218), perceived harmfulness (arXiv:2510.20956). Other constructions: in arXiv:2601.16034 the GLM-4.6V direction is a weighted sum of GLM-4.6V's own final-token mean-difference concept atoms (one of them red-teaming vs benign prompts), and only the weights come from donor Qwen3-VL-8B; SVD of the abliterated-minus-base weight difference (gh:pocharlies-org/deepseek-v4-flash-rank1-refusal-projection); multi-direction edits (arXiv:2608.17202, arXiv:2512.18901). Other site: gh:mandoof1/abliteration keeps a harmful-minus-harmless mean but takes it over generated response positions (also gh:mandoof1/wolfram, same owner and method); its prompt-final-token direction was inert.

In reasoning models removal is often partial or comes with incoherence. Examples: weight orthogonalization 81.2%->70.6% on Qwen3-4B* (arXiv:2604.02574); Ouro-2.6B-Thinking 0.950->0.890 (arXiv:2610.15218); 46/50->24/50 on MiniMax with thinking (gh:blackfrost-ai/blackfrost_ai_minimaxm31_rti); on GPT-OSS-20B the CoT-mean direction's 88% removal counts incoherent generations, so it is the rate before the coherence filter, which excludes exactly those cases (arXiv:2609.14759).

Induction often needs repeated or progress-aware application during decoding. A single-pass addition does not reach the output (arXiv:2608.08032: L18 log-prob -38.4->-39.7). Fixed-strength addition is partial (https://openreview.net/forum?id=TynYvwkSlF: 0.23->0.65 on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B), and some tests give a null (gh:natalimuca/jailbreak-activation-detection; arXiv:2609.03887 Qwen3-8B Ra-SFT 32.4->30.8).

Results are mixed. Kept: GLM-4.7-Flash (ARC-Challenge 61.86->62.80), GLM-4.6V (GSM8K 81.2->81.5) and R1-Distill-Llama-8B (MMLU 55.7->55.7). Lost: AIME/GPQA/BBEH generally 5-30% worse after CoT-direction ablation (arXiv:2507.03167), ARC-E 78.8->69.9 on Qwen3-4B* (arXiv:2604.02574), and MMLU-Pro engineering 76.88->67.70 on Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Thinking (arXiv:2512.16602).

method_sensitivity.factor: Direction extraction token (end of prompt or EOI, EOT, CoT tokens, last CoT token, response region)
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2507.03167 (refused-minus-complied directions; GPT-OSS-20B edited by per-expert weight orthogonalisation), GPT-OSS-20B: refusal on the full held-out set (n=487) 93.4%->3.5% with the CoT direction vs ->7.0% with end-of-prompt; non-completed generations on the common-refused subset (n=24) 2.4%->4.1% (CoT; coherence largely kept, checker reads observed) vs 2.4%->39.9% (end-of-prompt). gh:mandoof1/abliteration, MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B: prompt-final-token direction inert; response-region direction 78.1%->9.4% (variant D). arXiv:2609.14759, GPT-OSS-20B: end-of-prompt direction 4% coherent flips, last-CoT-token direction none. arXiv:2605.26772, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, one-layer negative activation addition with the original CoT fixed: compliance up to 39% (EOI-token direction) vs up to 43% (EOT-token direction), best layer, from 0%.

method_sensitivity.factor: Intervention placement, depth and schedule (single point vs all layers; single pass vs every decode step; hook layer; fixed vs progress-aware)
method_sensitivity.what: https://openreview.net/forum?id=ySFIGhpfDe: final-norm single-point ablation gives -1.3 to +2.5 pp on Qwen3-8B (no CIs), while all-layer ablation strongly affects Qwen (text, figure only). arXiv:2608.08032, Sarvam-30B, alpha=4: a single pass at L10 does not reach the L18 output (-38.4->-39.7); per-decode-step addition recovers 87% (L5), 93% (L8), 80% (L10), 47% (L12), 29% (L14) in the Appendix B sweep, though Section 4 gives 0.65 [0.50, 0.78] for the same L10 setting. https://openreview.net/forum?id=TynYvwkSlF, Qwen3-8B refusal (success; unclosed CoT, fractions; no steering 0.43; 0.04), Table 1 controls: progress-aware multi-layer SubSteer 0.98; 0.01, fixed strength 0.89; 0.10, single layer 0.39; 0.54. The same progress-aware schedule with the EOI direction gives 0.68; 0.00, equal to fixed-strength single-layer RD addition (0.68; 0.00). So RD and SubSteer differ in direction position as well as schedule.

gh:anki079/refusal-in-reasoning-models (README-only read), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, L22 direction, JBB-harmful: answer-only ablation is byte-for-byte identical to baseline, while think-only ablation matches full-rollout ablation. The README gives no refusal rates for full-rollout or think-only ablation, so the size of the phase effect cannot be read (the checker reads r7 as cannot_determine). Untreated JBB-harmful refusal is 15%.

arXiv:2605.28467, Qwen3-8B addition: 4.1% (alpha=1), 6.1% (alpha=2), 61.2% (alpha=5), 100.0% (alpha=10); subtraction 94.9% (alpha=1, 2), 58.2% (alpha=5), 1.2% (alpha=10). gh:pocharlies-org/deepseek-v4-flash-rank1-refusal-projection: 5/10 and 7/10 refusals at lambda=1, 0/10 at lambda=1.5 and 2. gh:blackfrost-ai/blackfrost_ai_minimaxm31_rti: alpha 1.5/1.6 gives more empty and looping answers than 1.4. https://openreview.net/forum?id=qSmUharVw6: collapse to no-final at alpha=+/-3.

arXiv:2605.26772, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, EOI steering: compliance 39% with the original CoT fixed, 70% with the CoT suppressed, 94% with the CoT regenerated (from 0%). gh:jcartu/glm5.2-unbound: edited GLM-5.2 refuses with thinking on but complies with thinking off plus a permissive system prompt. https://openreview.net/forum?id=ySFIGhpfDe, single-point (final-norm) ablation, Table 11, no CIs or tests: Qwen3-8B shows no mode effect (plain mean-difference -1.3 pp non-thinking, +2.5 pp thinking; sweeps -2.1 to 0.0 pp and -2.1 to +2.9 pp). On Gemma-4-12B the plain direction gives -2.9 pp in both modes. An adjusted Class A (1,1) direction gives +7.1 pp non-thinking vs +1.25 pp thinking, and the authors name non-thinking Gemma as the only exception to weak single-point effects.

method_sensitivity.factor: Derivation recipe and projection strength (single textbook direction vs banded multi-block or heretic-class; partial vs full projection)
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2608.17202: textbook single-direction derivation fails on Qwen3.5-27B/-9B (best compliance 0.4375; refusal never below about 0.25-0.31), while a banded two-block public recipe on Qwen3.5-122B reaches refusal 0.00 in both thinking modes. The study's method-sensitivity line says the textbook recipe worked on gemma-3-27b and Qwen3-14B. gh:drewstone/safety-is-a-policy, Qwen3.5-27B: partial projections 0% compliance, standard abliteration ~30%, full projections corrupted.

arXiv:2512.16602, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Thinking political refusal from 92.35%. On China-centric data: MD 33.24%, RMD 27.06%, WMD 55.00%, WRMD 47.35%. On Extended data: MD 58.82%, RMD 67.07%, WMD 33.73%, WRMD 23.82%.

arXiv:2507.03167, same models and interventions, two measures. Full held-out set (n=487), share of generations with mean StrongREJECT <0.4: falls to 0.4%-10.1%. The checker reads the highest, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B end-of-prompt 38.7%->10.1%, as partial (CoT direction on the same model: 0.4%). Common-refused subset (n=24, Table 7), mean StrongREJECT compliance: 0.294-0.888 (Llama-8B end-of-prompt 0.294, CoT 0.888). The verdict reads r2 and r5-r8 (0.294-0.604) as partial. GPT-OSS-20B end-of-prompt is 93.4%->7.0% on the first measure and 0.562 on the second; the second is depressed by 39.9% zero-padded incomplete generations (verdict fix). arXiv:2609.14759, GPT-OSS-20B, CoT-mean direction: the 88% refusal removal includes incoherent generations, so it is the rate before the coherence filter. The study counts only coherent flips, so the 88% does not count as success.

status_amendment.public_note: The reasoning-models status was revised after fact-checking: one model was taken off the list of disputed results because the failing result behind it was not a real test, the main supporting study is now marked as coming from the original authors' group, and facts from one paper that could not be checked are marked unverified. The level stays contested, because other groups using methods close to the original still fail to remove refusal in several reasoning models, although no success and failure on the same model used the same method.
